Color management in digital imaging requires conversion between device-dependent and device-independent color spaces. The workflow follows three (3) steps: (1) input profiling (characterizing the capture device, e.g., camera or scanner), (2) working space conversion (typically to a standard RGB space such as sRGB or Adobe RGB 1998), and (3) output profiling (mapping to the destination device, e.g., printer or display). ICC profiles (International Color Consortium, file extension .icc or .icm) encode the relationship between device color values and the profile connection space (PCS, defined as CIELAB or CIEXYZ). Rendering intents determine how out-of-gamut colors are handled: (a) perceptual (compresses entire gamut, preserving relative relationships), (b) relative colorimetric (clips out-of-gamut colors to nearest in-gamut equivalent), (c) saturation (prioritizes vivid colors, used for business graphics), and (d) absolute colorimetric (preserves exact colors including white point, used for proofing). Display calibration targets a white point of D65 (6500K), gamma of 2.2, and luminance of 120 cd/m2 (for standard viewing conditions per ISO 3664).
